findings.claim: POST /api/maps/:id/entities and POST /api/maps/:id/generate-entities call `await pool.connect()` OUTSIDE their try block, so a connection-acquisition failure escapes the async handler as an unhandledRejection and kills the whole Node process.
findings.failure_scenario: The Postgres container restarts (or max_connections is briefly exhausted) while an admin saves map entities. `pool.connect()` at index.js:580 rejects before the try block is entered; Express 4.18 does not catch async handler rejections, so the rejection reaches the process. Proven locally on Node 22.19 by injecting a pool whose connect() rejects: the HTTP request never gets a response (client aborts) and, with no unhandledRejection listener installed, the process terminates with a fatal uncaught-rejection trace pointing at index.js:580. Because attachAuthority() binds the WS authority to this same server (index.js:1394), the exit drops every connected player mid-session. index.js:653 has the identical shape.
findings.proposed_fix: Move `const client = await pool.connect()` inside the try block in both routes (initialise `let client = null` outside, and guard `client?.release()` in finally), matching the hardening already applied to backend/src/auth/middleware.js:35-43 for the same failure class. Consider also adding a process-level unhandledRejection handler that logs and responds rather than exiting.
findings.verification: Run the repo-local probe: require backend/src/index.js, __setPool({ query: async () => ({rows:[{token_version:1,role:"admin"}]}), connect: async () => { throw new Error("boom"); } }), then POST /api/maps/1/entities with a valid admin bearer token. Expect (current) process exit with an uncaught rejection at index.js:580; after the fix, expect HTTP 500 and the process still alive.

findings.claim: The three unauthenticated job-status proxies interpolate the raw :jobId path param into a URL path, so an encoded ../ traverses out of /jobs/ and reaches arbitrary GET endpoints on the internal sprite-gen service.
findings.failure_scenario: An unauthenticated caller requests GET /api/entity-jobs/..%2F..%2Fopenapi.json. Express decodes the param to "../../openapi.json"; spriteGen.getJob() builds fetch("http://sprite-gen:8100/jobs/../../openapi.json"); the URL parser normalises it to http://sprite-gen:8100/openapi.json. Confirmed live against localhost:13101 on 2026-07-24: the response was sprite-gen full OpenAPI schema (HTTP 200), and GET /api/tile-jobs/..%2Fcapability returned the host hardware profile. sprite-gen is not otherwise reachable from outside the compose network, and none of these three routes requires a token, so the public API is acting as an open unauthenticated GET proxy into the private service segment. Impact today is internal-API and host-capability disclosure; it becomes remote-trigger the moment sprite-gen gains any GET endpoint with a side effect.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate :jobId against the job-id format before use (e.g. reject anything not matching /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/ with 400) in all three proxies — /api/sprite-jobs/:jobId (745), /api/entity-jobs/:jobId (833), /api/tile-jobs/:jobId (894) — and encodeURIComponent it inside services/spriteGen.js:24 so the escape is closed at both layers. Decide separately whether these three routes should require auth at all.
findings.verification: curl -s "http://localhost:13101/api/tile-jobs/..%2Fcapability" with no Authorization header. Currently returns sprite-gen capability JSON with HTTP 200; after the fix expect HTTP 400 and no proxied body.

findings.claim: item_types.value (an item gold worth) is never written by POST or PUT /api/item-types and has no admin UI field, so every item type created after the merchant migration is permanently worth 0 gold.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin creates a new sword via the Item Types panel. The INSERT at index.js:360 omits the `value` column, so it takes the migration default 0 (backend/migrations/1714440032000_merchant_stock.js:6, notNull default 0). services/merchantStock.js:30 seeds a village base catalog with `WHERE category IN (weapon,armor) AND value > 0`, so the new sword can never appear in any merchant catalog; authority/trade.js:91 reads the same column for the sell price, so a player who loots it sells it for sellPriceFor(0) = 0 gold. There is no API route and no form field that can set `value` — the only remedy is a manual SQL UPDATE. Every item type shipped through the admin UI since that migration is affected.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `value` to the INSERT and UPDATE column lists in POST/PUT /api/item-types, validate it in validateItemType() as a non-negative finite integer (the same shape as the existing stamina_cost check at index.js:318), and add the field to ItemTypesAdmin.jsx. Backfill existing zero-value rows using the same expressions the migration used.
findings.verification: curl -s http://localhost:13101/api/item-types | jq '[.[] | {name, value}]' and confirm every row created through the admin UI has value 0; then create an item type via POST /api/item-types with {"value": 25} and confirm the returned row still reports value 0.

findings.claim: PUT /api/worlds/:id stores entry_spawn as any object without checking it lands inside the world bounds, and chooseSpawn() only checks Number.isFinite, so an out-of-range spawn puts every first-time joiner inside the solid wall ring.
findings.failure_scenario: A world is 24x24 tiles (valid coordinates 0..2400 px). In MapsAdmin the entry-spawn inputs (MapsAdmin.jsx:96-98) are plain number fields with no min/max, so an admin typing 99999 saves entry_spawn {x:99999,y:99999}. index.js:1032 accepts any object and writes it to jsonb unvalidated. On join, mapService.chooseSpawn() (line 588) only tests Number.isFinite and returns it verbatim; authority/server.js:206 uses it with no clamp. stampBounds() marks every tile outside the rectangle as map_wall, so every player joining that entry world for the first time materialises deep inside impassable wall with no in-game way out. The same gap lets a bounds shrink via PUT strand already-persisted world_players positions outside the new ring.
findings.proposed_fix: In PUT /api/worlds/:id validate entry_spawn.x/entry_spawn.y are finite numbers inside (0, width*100) x (0, height*100) and return 400 otherwise; when nextW/nextH shrink, also clamp or clear entry_spawn and any world_players rows now outside the ring. Mirror the min/max on the MapsAdmin inputs.
findings.verification: In the browser: set a bounded world as entry, type 99999 into both entry-spawn fields, Save (expect 400 after the fix; currently 200). Then join that world as a fresh player and confirm whether the avatar appears inside the wall and cannot move in any direction.

findings.claim: Entity types are referenced by NAME (not id) in worlds.allowed_creature_types and world_creatures.type, but PUT /api/entity-types/:id renames freely with no check on those references, silently orphaning them.
findings.failure_scenario: A world has allowed_creature_types ["Goblin"] and creature_count 40. An admin renames the Goblin entity type to "Goblin Scout" in the Entity Types panel. PUT /api/entity-types/:id (index.js:239) updates the row with no referential check. The next POST /api/worlds/:id/creatures runs `SELECT ... FROM entity_types WHERE is_creature = true AND name = ANY($1::text[])` (index.js:1120) with the stale ["Goblin"], matches zero rows, skips the placement block, and returns HTTP 200 {"placed": 0}. The admin sees a success toast and a world with no creatures, with no error surfaced anywhere. The same name coupling applies to the hardcoded GUARD_TYPE = "Village Guard" literal (index.js:1177) used by three DELETE statements: renaming that entity type makes the re-roll `WHERE type <> $2` guard-sparing clause stop matching, so a re-roll wipes every village guard.
findings.proposed_fix: Either block a rename that is referenced (check worlds.allowed_creature_types and world_creatures.type, return 409 with the referencing worlds) or cascade it inside one transaction (UPDATE worlds SET allowed_creature_types, UPDATE world_creatures SET type). Longer term, key allowed_creature_types and world_creatures.type on entity_types.id instead of name, and resolve GUARD_TYPE via faction = guard, which is how the authority already identifies guards (authority/creatures.js:66).
findings.verification: With a bounded world configured for one creature type: rename that entity type in the admin UI, then click Re-roll creatures and observe the response. Currently expect HTTP 200 with placed 0 and an empty map; after the fix expect a 409 on the rename or a re-roll that still places creatures.

findings.claim: seedBaseCatalog() is called only at village creation, so item types added later never enter any existing village merchant catalog and there is no re-seed endpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin creates village V in world W; seedBaseCatalog (index.js:1256) copies the item types that exist at that moment into merchant_stock. The admin then adds a new armour type. services/merchantStock.js fetchShop() reads merchant_stock only, and nothing ever re-runs the seed, so players trading at V never see the new armour — and every village created before the item existed is permanently missing it, while villages created afterwards have it. The only recovery is deleting and recreating the village (which cascades away its buyback rows) or a manual SQL insert.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an idempotent re-seed: an admin route (or a call on item-type create) that inserts the missing base-catalog rows for every village, e.g. the existing SELECT-INSERT plus `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM merchant_stock ms WHERE ms.village_id = $2 AND ms.item_type_id = item_types.id)`, and a matching delete/price-refresh when an item type is removed or repriced.
findings.verification: Create a village, then create a new weapon item type with value > 0, then read the shop for that village and confirm the new weapon is absent. After the fix it should appear without recreating the village.

findings.claim: Village create, village delete and creature re-roll each perform several dependent writes with no transaction, so a failure part-way leaves the world in a state the API cannot be asked to repair.
findings.failure_scenario: POST /api/worlds/:id/villages runs INSERT villages, then insertVillageGuards, then seedBaseCatalog, then invalidateWorld as four independent statements on the shared pool. If seedBaseCatalog throws (constraint error, transient DB fault), the village row and its guards are already committed but the shop is empty; the client gets HTTP 500 "Failed to create village" and the admin retries — and the retry is rejected with 400 "village overlaps an existing village" from the phantom village they were never told exists. DELETE /api/worlds/:id/villages/:villageId (index.js:1265) and POST /api/worlds/:id/creatures (index.js:1097) have the same shape around the guard wipe: they DELETE every world_creatures row of type Village Guard and then re-insert them, so a failure between the two leaves the world with zero guards and no endpoint that re-derives them except another creature re-roll.
findings.proposed_fix: Check out a client and wrap each of the three routes in BEGIN/COMMIT with ROLLBACK in catch and release in finally, exactly as POST /api/maps/:id/entities (index.js:579) already does — and move the connect() inside the try (see the P0 finding on the same pattern).
findings.verification: Point the backend at a pool whose merchant_stock INSERT fails, POST a village, then GET /api/worlds/:id/villages. Currently the village is listed despite the 500; after the fix the list should be unchanged.

findings.claim: creature_count has no server-side upper bound and the re-roll loop issues one round-trip INSERT per creature and a full generateRegion() per placement attempt, so a large count ties the request and a DB connection up indefinitely.
findings.failure_scenario: The Creatures field in MapsAdmin is <Input type="number" min="0"> with no max (MapsAdmin.jsx:79) and PUT /api/worlds/:id only clamps with Math.max(0, Math.floor(creature_count)) (index.js:1027). An admin typing 500000 and clicking Re-roll creatures makes index.js:1118 loop 500k times, each iteration calling generateRegion() for a 1x1 window up to 40 times (each of those rebuilds worldConfig and recomputes the whole coarse path lattice via collectPathCells), then issuing one individual INSERT per placed creature. The request has no timeout and never returns, holds a pool client for its duration, and grows world_creatures without limit — which the authority then loads into the world sim. POST /api/maps/generate (index.js:537) has the same class of gap: rows/cols default to 100 but are unvalidated, so {"rows":100000,"cols":100000} allocates a 10^10-cell grid and exhausts the heap.
findings.proposed_fix: Clamp creature_count server-side in PUT /api/worlds/:id (e.g. 0..2000, 400 above it) and add a max to the MapsAdmin input; batch the placement INSERTs into a single multi-row statement; hoist worldConfig()/collectPathCells() out of the per-attempt path by sampling a pre-generated region instead of calling generateRegion() per candidate tile. Apply the same numeric clamp to rows/cols in POST /api/maps/generate.
findings.verification: PUT /api/worlds/:id with creature_count 200000 (expect 400 after the fix; currently 200), then POST /api/worlds/:id/creatures and time it. Currently expect no response; after the fix expect a 400 at the PUT.

findings.claim: A 50 MB JSON/urlencoded body limit is installed globally, so it applies to every unauthenticated route, and no global rate limit exists — only /api/auth has one.
findings.failure_scenario: express.json({ limit: "50mb" }) at index.js:18 runs as app-level middleware, before routing and before any auth guard, so it parses bodies for unauthenticated paths too. An unauthenticated client POSTs 50 MB of JSON to /api/health (or any path, including ones with no route); the body is buffered and parsed before the 404 is produced. The only rate limiter in the surface is authRateLimiter() inside auth/routes.js:13, scoped to register/login, and cors() is installed with no origin restriction (index.js:17), so this is reachable from any origin without credentials. A modest number of concurrent such requests drives backend heap growth; because the WS authority shares the process (index.js:1394), a heap exhaustion drops every connected player. No route in this surface needs 50 MB: the largest legitimate body is the map entity array in POST /api/maps/:id/entities.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the global limit to something small (e.g. 256kb) and apply a larger per-route limit only where it is needed, e.g. app.post("/api/maps/:id/entities", adminGuard, express.json({ limit: "10mb" }), handler). Add a modest global rate limiter in front of the router.
findings.verification: head -c 52000000 /dev/zero | tr "\0" "a" into a JSON string file, then run 20 concurrent unauthenticated `curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @big.json http://localhost:13101/api/health` and watch the backend container RSS. Currently expect large RSS growth per in-flight request; after the fix expect HTTP 413 immediately.

findings.claim: generateWFC() has no caller anywhere outside its own unit tests, yet the tile_types.valid_neighbors column it is the sole consumer of is still a curated, required field in the Tile Types admin UI.
findings.failure_scenario: generateWFC (mapService.js:1-72) and densityAt (mapService.js:337) have zero non-test references in backend/src or frontend/src; world generation goes through generateWorld/generateRegion instead. mapService.js:47 is the only read of validNeighbors in the codebase. TileTypesAdmin.jsx:583 still renders a full checkbox grid for valid_neighbors, POST/PUT /api/tile-types (index.js:467, 488) still persist it, and getTileTypesMap (index.js:91) still ships it to the client. So an admin who spends time curating adjacency rules for every tile type changes nothing about any generated map, and the UI gives no hint of that. The dead generator also keeps its own test suite green, so a change to hash2/globalValueNoise/worldConfig must keep code no product flow reaches passing.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide the product question, then act on it: either delete generateWFC, densityAt, the valid_neighbors editor and (via migration) the column; or wire generateWorld to honour valid_neighbors so the admin input has an effect. Do not leave the field editable while nothing reads it.
findings.verification: Set valid_neighbors on two tile types so they are mutually exclusive, then POST /api/maps/generate and inspect the returned grid for adjacent occurrences of the two. Currently expect them adjacent (the rule is ignored).

findings.claim: The three generation-job routes and the four approve routes are near-verbatim copies that differ only in a kind string and a default frame count, and one copy has already drifted.
findings.failure_scenario: POST /api/sprite-jobs (718), /api/entity-jobs (808) and /api/tile-jobs (869) are identical 20-line blocks apart from kind and the chosenFrames default (4 vs 1 vs 1), including the tier auto-select fallback and the sprite_sets INSERT — so the jobId validation the security finding calls for, or any concurrency cap on this CPU-bound work, must be written three times to be correct. The four approve routes have already drifted: POST /api/entity-types/:id/image clears sprite = NULL with a comment explaining that the atlas path otherwise keeps winning, while POST /api/tile-types/:id/image (904) leaves sprite populated; that is harmless only because resolveTileVisual gates on render_mode === animated rather than on sprite presence, so it is a trap waiting for the tile renderer to adopt the entity precedence rule. job_id handling also differs: three routes treat it as optional, /api/entity-types/:id/sprite (774) 404s without it.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract one startGenerationJob({ subject, kind, defaultFrames, req, res }) helper for the three job routes and one approveGenerated({ table, mode, ... }) helper for the approve routes, so validation, tier fallback and the sprite/image precedence rule exist once. Make the tile image approval clear sprite the way the entity one does, so the two agree.
findings.verification: After extraction, POST each of the three job routes with a jobless payload and confirm identical validation behaviour; approve a tile image over an existing animated tile and confirm tile_types.sprite is NULL.
